Begoña Morenes
Global Head of Investor Relations, Banco Santander
Good morning, everybody, and welcome to Banco Santander's Conference to discuss our financial results for H1 2022. Just as a reminder, both the results report and the presentation we will be following today are available to you on our website. I'm joined here today by our CEO, Mr. José Antonio Álvarez, and our CFO, Mr. José García Cantera. Following their presentations, we will open the floor for any questions you may have in the Q&A session. With this, I will hand over to Mr. José Antonio Álvarez. José Antonio, the floor is yours.
José Antonio Álvarez
CEO, Banco Santander
Thank you, Begoña. Good morning to everyone. Thank you for joining us this morning. Well, I should start saying that Q2, we've been living in a period in which we saw inflation hitting decade-high levels, interest rates going up, starting to rise, and significant concerns regarding lower economic activity in the future. This is to sum up a little bit the environment of the last quarter. In this environment, we continue to grow our business, our customer base, and we translate this into a growth in the loans and deposits and revenues in our P&L, NII plus fees, as you can see in the slide. The progress in the digital front has been significant in the quarter.
When we talk about profitability, Q2 profit was EUR 2.4 billion, for the H1 reaching EUR 4.9 billion, 33% higher than the previous year. If we look at the cost in euros is 21% higher than the previous year. The cost in a highly inflationary environment remain well below inflation, and our efficiency ratios stood at 45.5% in line to reach our end of the year target of 45%. We improve our profitability ratios, the return on tangible equity stays at 13.7%, and we continue to create significant value per share for our shareholders. EPS grew 38% compared to the previous year, and tangible net asset value per share plus cash dividend per share grew 9% year-on-year.
In regard with this trend, the quality of the balance sheet NPLs continue to trend down. The cost of risk remain well inside our expected range and our capital is slightly above 12%, the Common Equity Tier 1, following a strong net organic generation of 18 basis points in Q2. I have just mentioned, our commercial strategy were reflected in widespread growth. As you can see in the slide, we've been growing in individuals, both in mortgages, consumer, and others in mid to high single digits. Less so in the corporate space, where we are seeing relatively flat this loan book in SMEs and corporates, while CIB is growing at 13%.
Overall, loans were up 2% quarter-on-quarter, EUR 21 billion in the quarter, which increases in all countries, mainly from mortgages and consumers, as I said. In summary, I think we have a high quality, well-diversified portfolio by market, and our CFO, José, will explain later on in more detail the portfolio by geographies and by collateral. On the other hand, deposits grew 1% quarter-on-quarter and 5% year-on-year, with a market shift towards time deposits due to the interest, the new interest rate environment. Turning to the income statement, well, let me first give you a brief overview of the main ideas.
The performance in euros was better than in the currencies due to the depreciation of the euros, although we have a negative partially offset by the hedging included in the corporate center. This is included in gains on financial transactions. In constant euros, talking in constant euros, group grew revenue 4% year-on-year at a faster pace than in Q1 on the back of higher volumes, interest rate hikes starting to feed through in some countries, together with another strong quarter in CIB. Cost management faced inflationary pressures but continued to grow well below inflation. This allow us to achieve record pre-provision profit of EUR 14 billion in the H1 of this year. As for loan loss provisions, the releases recorded in the UK and US in Q2 2021 affected the year-on-year comparison.
Finally, we had a positive impact from minority interests, following buybacks in Mexico and the US, and lower tax burden mainly in Brazil due to the recovery from tax contingencies and others. This led to a record H1 profit of EUR 4.9 billion in 2022. Attributable underlying profit recorded the same amount as we don't have extraordinary charges in this H1. If we look for areas in Europe, we continue to accelerate our business transformation towards a common operating model. These were reflected in a customer growth year-on-year, increasing nearly by 300,000 in the quarter. Double-digit growth in net operating income and profit. Return on tangible equity improved to 8.8%. In North America, we are refocusing our position in the US while maintaining a disciplined capital allocation. We accelerate growth volumes.
Loans rose 7% in most segments in Mexico, and in auto and CIB in the US. We also increased our customer base 3% year-on-year. Lastly, we achieved a profit of EUR 1.6 billion in the region. South America, we are leaders in the region with a unique presence strengthened by the group assets and delivering profitable growth. Our growth strategy based on increasing customers, EUR 6 million year-on-year, and capturing new business opportunities led to a sharp increase in volumes. Loans growth 12% and deposits 5%. H1 underlying profit over EUR 1.9 billion, 7% year-on-year, and higher return on tangible equity reaching, staying above 20%. In Digital Consumer Bank, we continue to strengthen our leadership position, as reflected in new lending. We rose 10%, by 10% in a shrinking market.
Profit rose to double digits, and return on tangible equity is increased to 12%. If we look at performance metrics, efficiency ratio, I already elaborate on this. We are running at 45.5%. Now, heading towards our target of 45% for the year end. Return on tangible equity, we are slightly ahead of our target for the whole year, 13.7%. We are on track to meet our 2022 target. In terms of EPS, EUR 0.27 in the quarter, 38% year-on-year, 19% versus H1 2021 in underlying earnings per share. We are showing sustained earnings per share growth.
Mainly if we take into account that we amortize 500, almost 550 million shares through the buybacks, that is approximately 3%, slightly above 3%, 3.2% of our capital. The tangible net asset value per share was EUR 4.24, including cash and dividends. It was in line with the previous quarter and 9% higher year-on-year. When it comes to capital, the organic capital generation was in line with our expectations. Net organic 18 basis points. If we take into account the payout of 40% half in cash dividend, half in buyback, we are generating, roughly speaking, 10 after taking into consideration the buyback. That is in line with our expectations then per quarter.
This quarter does not show up in the total capital ratio due to the fact that held to collect and sell. The mark-to-market detracts 13 basis points on our capital, and this offset the growth in the organic generation. We are meeting our targets here. Risk-weighted assets growth below loan growth. We show that this is one of our target. Better profitability in the front book and reducing the weight of risk-weighted assets that are producing a return on equity below the cost of equity. We are progressing well on those targets, and this shows in our profitability. Finally, before I hand to José, I would like to highlight Santander's strong commitments in ESG.
Mainly, I want to refer to new targets we published just a couple of weeks ago, on top of the already existing targets in relation with power generation and coal. We published specific targets for energy, aviation and still reduce the absolute level of emissions in the region of 30% for the relevant period from 2019 to 2030. Well, you have the figures on, we are progressing in green finance, and we appointed a new head of green finance in order to first measure properly, to classify properly according to EU taxonomy, our loan book, and to generate a business, and help our customer to a greener economy for all our customers.
Well, as you know, we have, we are very active in the social front, particularly in Latin America, with financially empowered people. You have the figures in the presentation. Overall, I'm proud of the Group progress on delivering on our responsible banking commitments to help to tackle global challenges, both in the climate front and in the social front. I will now hand to José to elaborate on the Group and business area review. Finally, I will do some final remarks.
José García Cantera
CFO and Senior EVP, Banco Santander
Thank you, Antonio. Good morning, everyone. The CEO just provided a brief overview of the main highlights for the quarter, and I will go into more detail about the P&L of the group and the progress of the country and business areas. In the quarter, we earned EUR 2.4 billion after recording regulatory charges of nearly EUR 500 million, EUR 400 million for the resolution fund and EUR 88 million contribution to the new Institutional Protection Scheme in Poland. In the H1, total income exceeded EUR 25 billion. Both NII and fee income grew at 7% in constant euros and accounted for 97% of total income.
Trading gains and other income decreased 40%, compared to last year, mostly affected by FX hedging, which detracted EUR 300 million, and also from lower lease income, ALCO portfolio sales in 2021, and higher regulatory contributions. In the quarterly performance, we saw similar trends, revenue up 4%, excluding regulatory charges. Let me take a moment to go through the main drivers of NII in more detail. Group NII was up supported by broad-based growth in loans and deposits, coupled with margin management and interest rate hikes in UK and Poland. As a result, Net interest margin increased from 2.38% last year to 2.49% in H1 of this year. You have all the information on the slide, but I would like to highlight the following by country.
We had very strong NII in the UK and Poland, as I mentioned, because these are the two countries where we see the impact of higher rates in Europe. We also had robust activity in both countries. In Spain and Poland, we decreased NII by 6% and 8% respectively, despite the rise in volumes, due to the continued pressure on yields and lower ALCO portfolios. In the US, NII was affected by the Bluestem portfolio disposal and consumer loan pricing competition. In Mexico, NII up 9% due to strong loan growth in individuals and corporates. Finally, in Brazil, NII rose 2% backed by volume growth and credit mix, which was particularly offset by negative sensitivity to initial rate hikes.
We expect this negative impact from liability repricing to level out in Q4 of this year and turn positive into next year. Regarding fees, we had very positive performance in all regions, supported by greater activity in high value added products and services, as you can see on the right-hand side of the slide. All countries increased the income with the exception of the UK, which was affected by the transfer of the CIB business to the London branch. It would have been flattish, excluding this impact, and in the US, affected by the Bluestem disposal and lower overdraft fees. In terms of costs, we kept our target of growing costs below inflation while improving the efficiency. In Europe, costs were down 7% in real terms, with widespread falls across countries, and the efficiency here improved four percentage points.
In summary, we continue to make structural changes to our operating model to drive new productivity improvements in the future. Turning to risk, the group maintained positive credit quality ratios. NPL, the NPL ratio was 3.05%, 21 basis points better than in the quarter, than in the previous quarter, and most markets improved. In Spain, it fell 64 basis points due to portfolio sales. Total loan loss reserves stood at EUR 24 billion, and the loan loss coverage at 71%, up two percentage points in the quarter. The distribution of the loan portfolio by stages remains stable, and even Stage 3 assets were lower in the quarter. Our cost of credit stood at 83 basis points. This is last twelve months.
If we look at H1, the cost of risk was 91 basis points in line with our target for the year. I would like to drill a little deeper into loan loss provisions and cost of risk performance. By country in Europe, all countries remain below 1% or were negative. In Spain, cost of risk improved due to lower loan loss provisions and better portfolio quality. UK and Portugal, slightly positive, considering only six months. In Poland, improved provisions, BAU provisions, but cost of risk was affected by the contribution to the Swiss franc mortgage portfolio. The US cost of risk below 1%. After the 2021 releases, loan loss provisions are up year-on-year, but still well below pre-pandemic levels.
In Mexico, cost of risk improved slightly, I mean, significantly, thanks to a better than expected performance of the loan portfolio. In Brazil, the cost of risk increased primarily in our secured individuals, which represents around 20% of the portfolio. Secured individuals, SMEs, and corporates, which represent 80% of the total portfolio, were stable. The coverage ratio over 90 days is well above pre-pandemic levels. We are better positioned than in the previous crisis. As we increase the individual secured portfolio, we have less volatility than the market, and cheque especial decreases its weight compared to previous crisis. In Digital Consumer, cost of risk improved and continued to show outstanding low levels considering the nature of the business. Finally, I would like to show you a brief overview of our loan portfolio. It's most concentrated in mature markets, around 80%.
In developing markets, Brazil accounts for just 9% of the group total, and 65% of the total portfolio is secured, mostly by real estate collateral. By segment, mortgages with loan-to-value below 80% account for 90% of the total. The consumer lending portfolio is very well collateralized and is a very short-term duration. SMEs and corporate is covered with 50% real guarantees. Lastly, 65% of our S, of our corporate portfolio, large corporate portfolio, is rated investment grade. 42% is rated above A-, a very good quality portfolio. Let me now make some brief comments about the evolution of our main units in 2022. In Spain, year-on-year results were driven by lower costs, 4%, and reduced cost of risk in an environment of weak revenue performance.
Looking forward, we expect trends to continue for H2. NII should absorb the impact of TLTRO cancellations, but in 2023, we expect to reflect asset repricing delivering margin expansion. Fee income should remain robust in H2. Costs should maintain its downward trend, pointing to achievement of our cost-to-income target. Cost of risk is expected to remain around 55 to 60 basis points for the year. In the UK, we also maintain very positive dynamics in new lending and strong NII. Looking forward, we expect these trends to continue, with NII growing well, although probably at lower rates than until today, flat costs, and cost of risk normalization close to around 10 basis points. In the United States, results compares 2022 results compared to high financials in 2021.
Nevertheless, in the H1, profit remained very high, above EUR 1 billion. Our outlook for 2022 is lower revenue impacted by lease businesses. Costs slightly up, partially due to the incorporations, the incorporation of Amherst Pierpont, and better than initially anticipated cost of risk well below normalized levels. Santander Mexico had another excellent quarter. For the year as a whole, we expect higher NII and fees, cost up impacted by investments in digitalization and higher inflation, and cost of risk below 2.5%, supporting a credit quality that is better than average.
In Brazil, in the H1, when we had a negative impact due to our balance sheet's initial negative sensitivity to higher rates, higher inflation that is putting pressure on costs, and a cost of risk that deteriorated in unsecured loans to individuals, we earn a 21.5% return on tangible equity. We expect to end 2022 maintaining efficiency around 30% and cost of risk below 4% to 4.5%, which will result in a return on equity around 20%. All in all, in a difficult year, we expect a strong set of results and profitability, and we are optimistic for 2023, when we expect to see an improvement in revenue. In the Digital Consumer Bank, new business activity increased 10% year-on-year. We gained market share, particularly in used cars.
Looking forward to H2, the environment will continue to be challenging, but we are confident in meeting our goals and expect a record year in new business, exceeding the previous record of EUR 49 billion in 2019. We expect some normalization from the current low cost of risk rate, but should remain well below previous normalized levels, because in this case, cost of risk has to do more with unemployment than with interest rates, and we expect a strong labor market in Europe in general in the coming years. CIB delivered another very strong, excellent quarter. In the coming quarters, we expect to continue to gain market share, increasing revenue through excellent dynamics in structured finance and project finance, transaction volumes, and markets where we are protecting the value of our trading books.
Wealth management and insurance, despite market volatility, results grew 15%. In private banking, we had net new money inflows of EUR 6 billion. In asset management, profits rose 8%. In insurance, gross written premiums rose 17%. Looking forward, we expect to maintain double-digit growth in profit contribution across the three businesses. In PagoNxt, total revenue in H1 surged 87% year on year on the back of our four main business segments, especially merchants and trade. Activity is evolving very well, and we believe we will meet our +50% revenue target for the whole year. Finally, in cards, we managed 96 million cards throughout the group, and revenue grew 28% year-on-year to circa EUR 2 billion. That, with double-digit growth in Latin America and Europe.
We expect to continue to grow turnover and revenue at high double digits in the coming months. Let me now turn it back to José Antonio Álvarez for his closing remarks.
José Antonio Álvarez
CEO, Banco Santander
Thank you, José. Let me try to guide you to take a look forward, how do we see the group evolving, in the coming quarters. On one side, on the revenue side, we have an environment in which, NII should increase in the coming quarters, benefiting mainly from interest rate hikes. Normally, the interest rate hikes take a while to show up in the P&L. It starts and accelerate later on. With the expected activity levels, we expect a significant acceleration of the revenues, particularly in 2023. You will see some of this. You are already seeing some of this clearly in Poland and UK, where the rates start to go up faster.
We will see next year, basically, a strong acceleration, significant acceleration on the back of high rates in the Eurozone and also in Mexico and in other countries. Fee income, José mentioned how our fee income generating business are evolving. You saw both wealth management and insurance and CIB that are the main fee income generators. We are gaining share clearly in CIB space. That is performing very well, and we are also doing very well in private banking and insurance, where we think that we can grow in wealth management and insurance well into double digits. For that reason, I am relatively optimistic about the commercial activity, fee income that generates fee income, positive in revenues and costs.
While we face clearly a higher inflation than the one we were expecting. While we have a track record and we continue to think that we're gonna be able to increase the productivity and to evolve really the cost well below inflation as we are doing quarter-after-quarter. Naturally, some of the inflation is gonna go through the cost base, particularly in those countries with high inflation. We feel that productivity gains and cost management will allow us cost grow well below inflation. In asset quality in this environment, as you know, IMF published some numbers yesterday or the day before yesterday, I don't remember exactly, and where there is an erosion of the expectations on the GDP.
Naturally, in this environment, the discussion is if there is a recession coming or not. Some of this credit quality duration, as you know, IFRS 9 requires us to anticipate potential deterioration. In H1 of the year, we already done in our provisions some of this, around EUR 600 million or something like that, for the duration. We see our given our loan portfolio structure, the high household saving rates, the low unemployment rates, and the resilient real estate prices as a protection in our portfolio. For this year, we feel comfortable that we're gonna be inside our range that we gave to you, less than 1%. We are running at 91 basis points, and we feel comfortable with our target for the year.
In our capital, our commitment is to stay at or above 12% in every quarter and having disciplined capital allocation, and well reflect this in the higher profitability. So, we are there. The capital generation of the group, other than the mark to market of held to collect and sell, has been good in the quarter. My impression is that continue to be good, and we continue generating capital on a continuous basis. This will translate into to our shareholders, where our commitment is to have a 40% payout for this year. Although, we hope to increase closer to 50% in the future, once the. That is what we communicate to you in our shareholder meeting.
Well, just to reiterate our commitments for the year, both in terms of efficiency, return on tangible equity, and Common Equity Tier 1, we feel comfortable. We feel that we can reach those targets this year. For the future, I think that the revenue increase will more than offset the potential higher costs and potential increase on cost of risk. I'm positive on the capacity of the group to generate profits in the future. That's it. Now we remain at your disposal for the questions you may have.
Begoña Morenes
Global Head of Investor Relations, Banco Santander
Thank you, José Antonio. We'll open now the floor for any questions.
Operator
We already have our first question from Ignacio Ulargui from BNP Paribas Exane. Please go ahead.
José Antonio Álvarez
CEO, Banco Santander
Ignacio, you there?
Operator
No. Our next question is coming from Alvaro Serrano from Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.
Alvaro Serrano
Managing Director and Equity Research Analyst, Morgan Stanley
Hi. Hi, good morning. Hopefully you can hear me. I've got two questions, one on Brazil and another clarification on your last comments on capital. On Brazil, I heard José mention that you keep the 4% to 4.5% cost of risk. If I look at Q2 standalone, cost of risk, I think is 525 basis points. And it looks like to achieve your guidance for the full year in the H2, you'd need to be below 400 basis points.
I just wanna make sure I've understood the guidance correctly, and maybe you can give a color, a bit of color of what's going on, because it's probably a steeper increase than we were expecting, although you had flagged that the peak would be in Q2. Maybe a bit of color of what's going on and if I got those numbers right. The second question on capital. The 50% you mentioned, José Antonio, is that? Can we expect that already in 2023?
Or another way to ask it, is there anything we need to take into account that might prevent you from raising it to 50%, i.e., remaining capital headwinds, I think for 2020 you already said there isn't any left, but I don't know if there's anything in the H2, conscious that Banamex is no longer on the table, so I just can't see any reason why you shouldn't increase it to 50%. Thank you.
José Antonio Álvarez
CEO, Banco Santander
Okay. Thanks Alvaro, for your questions on Brazil. Well, José already elaborate on this. Let me to go into more details. As José said, we are seeing an increasing cost of raising the consumer mass market portfolio. As you rightly said, in Q2 was higher than in Q1. Having said that, we remain comfortable with the guidance we gave to you. It's true that we saw already in June better results than we saw in the three or four previous months. We remain constructive, and we think that we are in control of this and this to remain in this range. As you know, we reduced the lending last year.
José already mentioned that our exposure to the overdraft, that is the part of the higher cost of risk has been reduced, and we feel comfortable with our expectations for the year. Mainly, take into account that Brazil has been one of the few countries in which expectations for GDP growth have been improved by the IMF. Yeah, so the situation in the country is true that we face elections by October, but in general, we see the situation from a more constructive point of view, and we think that with the measures we took and with the trends we are seeing, we're gonna stick with this for 4.5% cost of risk for the whole year.
We are not seeing any sign of deterioration other than the ones we saw before, so we are seeing the corporate book performing very well. We are seeing, including SMEs, and it remains related with the individual consumer portfolio. Inside the consumer, the auto portfolio improves already; it's more the unsecured consumer that is still causing this spike in the cost of risk. Second question, well, it's true that we said that we don't have headwinds going forward in our capital, while what I'm stating here is what we state in the AGM, the intention of the board to go to 50%. When is this gonna happen? Well, it's up to the board.
I am not in a position to anticipate the decision that is gonna be taken by the board, but this is the clear intention of the group is to go back to these levels and continue to use the buybacks and the combination of buybacks and cash dividend as we've done in the last year.
José García Cantera
CFO and Senior EVP, Banco Santander
If I may give you a bit of color about the regulatory charges in the H2. In the H1, we had five basis points in the Q1. The plus three in the Q2 has two components, each plus seven from the non-performing loan backstop difference and minus four from models, so from pure regulatory, we have around nine, 10 basis points already accounted for, and we would expect another 10, 15 in the H2. Very much in line with the guidance we gave you at the beginning of the year for 20 or 25 basis points total regulatory charges in the year as a whole.
Alvaro Serrano
Managing Director and Equity Research Analyst, Morgan Stanley
Okay. Thank you for the clarification, José.
Begoña Morenes
Global Head of Investor Relations, Banco Santander
Thank you, Alvaro. Can we have the next question, please?
Operator
The next question is coming from Ignacio Ulargui. Please go ahead.
Ignacio Ulargui
Iberian Banks Analyst, BNP Paribas Exane
Hi. You hear me now?
José Antonio Álvarez
CEO, Banco Santander
Very well, indeed.
Ignacio Ulargui
Iberian Banks Analyst, BNP Paribas Exane
Okay, perfect. Thanks so much. Sorry for the problem before. Just have one follow-up question on Mexico. Just following the sort of like the outcome of Banamex, what is the strategy that you plan to follow there, and what are the priorities for the bank in terms of organic growth? In which segments you think that you can gain market share? The other question is on cost of risk at a group level. I mean, you have given a bit of a comfort about Brazil. I mean, is there sort of like any other market where you think that there could be sort of like where you envisage some deterioration that could put at risk that below 100 basis points cost of risk guidance for 2022? Thank you.
José Antonio Álvarez
CEO, Banco Santander
Okay. Thank you, Ignacio, for your question. Mexico, what the strategy? Well, as you say, rightly said, and we communicate to the market, our strategy is to organic growth. When we look at our franchise in Mexico, we have overall 13% to 14% market share, enough scale to compete efficiently in a market, and no doubt about this. When you look in more detail where we're gonna focus, we're gonna focus more on individuals.
When you look at the market shares all across, it is true that our market share in the corporate space is higher than it is in the individual space, particularly for the reason the organic growth is gonna be focusing on growing the individual customer base, that should flow through in the balance sheet through a larger deposit base, individual deposit base, I mean, and through a large share, particularly on the consumer. We are growing in auto. We started three years ago.
We got already 14% market share, and we're gonna continue to grow in the consumer space, but also in credit cards, where we launched in September last year a new card that is selling 100,000 cards a month, and we are growing well there, and we expect the growth to accelerate. It's accelerating. If you look at the numbers, at the balance sheet, at the P&L, it's accelerating, and we expect to continue to this acceleration. In short, we're gonna focus more on the individual side, where we need to grow the deposit base and also in the consumer finance space and credit cards. In the mortgage market, our market share is around 18%, 19%. We are well above our average market. We are doing well there.
Those are gonna be the focus. It reminds me a little bit of the situation we faced in Brazil a couple of years ago when Bradesco bought HSBC. On the back of this, we were able to gain two or three percentage points of market share in Brazil in a very difficult time in Brazil at that time. Brazil was in recession at that time, and we were able to profit from this situation, and we expect, we are doing already on the back of the process now, and we expect to continue to do in the coming years. Second question, cost of risk, more general question, not that much focused in Brazil as your colleague, Alvaro. I already elaborated on Brazil. You mentioned other markets.
The cost of risk is going up in Brazil for the situation I explained, and it's going up also in the US. It's back to normal in the US. Yeah, in the US, the in 2021, the cost of risk was abnormally low, well below expected across the cycle, and we are in some kind of normalization. It's going according to our plans in a... Well, you know that the cost of risk largely depends on the auto market, and the auto market remains in a situation that is not, I don't know how to qualify, not normal, in the sense that the availability of new cars is not there, and the used car price remain at all-time highs, I think. This situation creates a market where the cost of risk is still up, and unemployment is very low.
Well, inflation helps to pay the bills in the short run, this will keep, for the time being, the normalization is gonna happen little by little in the US. This is the other market in which you go to the numbers, you see the cost of risk going up. In all the other markets, I don't see any sign of deterioration, quite the opposite. In Spain, we are trending down. We expect to continue to go down this year and next year. While in consumer, we are not seeing any sign across the board. I'm referring now to consumer in Europe. In Mexico, we feel very comfortable with the portfolio. In Chile, we also feel very comfortable with the portfolio.
I don't see any deterioration in the portfolios. In fact, NPLs are trending down. Remember that the NPLs now around 3%, taking into account that there is a change in criteria with the new definition of default. Like for like, we are compared with last year at this period around 2.8%, 2.8-something. Still trending down, we are not seeing signs of deterioration there. Well, maybe I should elaborate, because I mentioned in the previous quarters around ICO loans. Remember that in the previous quarter, we were discussing uncertainty surrounding ICO loans with the extension we did last year, for one year. Those loans mature, start to pay normal installments in April, May.
I should say it came significantly or much better than expected. Arrears, initial arrears were below 3%, and this is a significantly better than at least my expectations, yeah, and the uncertainty why I was showing you this. That's the situation. Our models have high sensitivity. As you know, we provide for based on IFRS and the models applying IFRS 9 rules. I mentioned that provisions in H1, EUR 600 million, were due to macro conditions, changing to picking the new macro conditions, so for the future. These were mainly in Spain, like EUR 100 million due to macro conditions. In UK, like EUR 250 million, and in US, EUR 130 million.
Those are provisions that are there due to change in the macro conditions, not reflecting any kind of deterioration in the portfolio. I think I expect to clarify a little bit the issue of the cost of risk.
Begoña Morenes
Global Head of Investor Relations, Banco Santander
Thank you. Thank you, Ignacio. Can we have the next question, please?
Operator
The next question is coming from Pamela Zuluaga from Credit Suisse.
Pamela Zuluaga
Equity Research Analyst, Credit Suisse
Good morning. Thank you for taking my questions. The first one is again around capital. Most of the organic capital that you keep on generating has been offset by fair valuation adjustments from your bond portfolios. Are you thinking about maybe changing your risk allocation strategy, shifting your accounting towards held-to-maturity for bonds in order to somehow shield capital better?
